title: 08. GraphRAG: Entity Linking & Disambiguation
summary: Entity Linking (EL) — also called Named Entity Disambiguation (NED) — is the process of mapping entity mentions in text to specific entries in a knowledge base.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: **Entity Linking (EL)** — also called **Named Entity Disambiguation (NED)** — is the process of mapping entity mentions in text to specific entries in a knowledge base. It solves two problems: (1) **surface form variation** — "Apple", "Apple Inc.", "AAPL", "Tim Cook's company" all refer to the same entity; (2) **ambiguity** — "Jordan" could be Michael Jordan, Jordan (country), Jordan (river), or Jordan Peterson. The EL pipeline: **NER** (identify spans) → **candidate generation** (find possible KB entries) → **disambiguation** (select correct one). Production EL systems: **BLINK** (Facebook, bi-encoder cross-encoder), **REL** (Radboud University, modular), **ReFinED** (Amazon, mention detection + entity disambiguation). In Graph RAG, EL is the critical bridge between raw query text and graph traversal — poor entity linking propagates errors throughout the entire retrieval pipeline.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
         ENTITY LINKING PIPELINE FOR GRAPH RAG

  INPUT TEXT
  "Apple's CEO Tim Cook announced iPhone sales in China exceeded Samsung."

  STAGE 1: MENTION DETECTION (spaCy NER)
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Spans: [Apple, ORG] [Tim Cook, PERSON] [iPhone, ORG] │
  │         [China, GPE] [Samsung, ORG]                    │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        ▼
  STAGE 2: CANDIDATE GENERATION
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  "Apple" candidates:                                   │
  │    1. Apple Inc.      (score: 0.98 — exact alias)     │
  │    2. Apple Records   (score: 0.72 — fuzzy)           │
  │    3. Apple TV+       (score: 0.65 — fuzzy)           │
  │                                                        │
  │  "Tim Cook" candidates:                                │
  │    1. Tim Cook [Apple CEO] (score: 1.0 — exact)       │
  │                                                        │
  │  "Samsung" candidates:                                 │
  │    1. Samsung Electronics (score: 0.95)               │
  │    2. Samsung Group       (score: 0.87)               │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        ▼
  STAGE 3: DISAMBIGUATION (BLINK bi-encoder → cross-encoder)
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                        │
  │  Bi-encoder (fast, coarse):                           │
  │  Query: "Apple CEO Tim Cook iPhone sales ..."          │
  │  → Top-64 candidates from FAISS                       │
  │                                                        │
  │  Cross-encoder (slow, precise):                       │
  │  [Context] [Apple] → [Apple Inc. description]         │
  │  Score: 0.94 → LINKED to Apple Inc.                   │
  │                                                        │
  │  Domain prior override:                                │
  │  "Apple" in financial context → Apple Inc. (0.99)     │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        ▼
  LINKED ENTITIES → GRAPH SEEDS
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Apple Inc.        → [Node in KG] → BFS expansion     │
  │  Tim Cook          → [Node in KG] → BFS expansion     │
  │  iPhone            → [Node in KG] → BFS expansion     │
  │  China             → [Node in KG] → BFS expansion     │
  │  Samsung Electronics → [Node in KG] → BFS expansion   │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  DISAMBIGUATION STRATEGIES
  ┌────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────┐
  │ "Jordan" context   │ Top signal        │ → Entity      │
  ├────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────┤
  │ "basketball"       │ NBA, Bulls        │ Michael Jordan│
  │ "Amman, capital"   │ country, diplomat │ Jordan country│
  │ "river, baptism"   │ biblical, water   │ Jordan River  │
  │ "psychology, book" │ professor, rules  │ Jordan Peterson│
  └────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────┘
```

quiz.question: What are the three stages of a production entity linking pipeline?
options: The NIL problem: entity mentions that don't match any entry in the KB should be marked as NIL (not-in-KB) rather than incorrectly linked to a wrong entity.
S1. SCENARIO: "Apple" links to "Apple Records" in a financial document — wrong entity.
ReFinED integrates mention detection and disambiguation in a single end-to-end model, while BLINK treats them separately.
(1) Mention Detection (NER): identify entity spans in text using spaCy, BERT-NER, or LLM; output: [(mention_text, start, end, entity_type), ...].
quiz.explanation: (1) Mention Detection (NER): identify entity spans in text using spaCy, BERT-NER, or LLM; output: [(mention_text, start, end, entity_type), ...]. (2) Candidate Generation: for each mention, retrieve candidate entities from KB using exact match, alias tables, BM25, or embedding similarity; output: top-k candidates per mention.

quiz.explanation: BLINK (Bi-encoder Entity Linking) uses a two-stage retrieval approach: (1) Bi-encoder stage: encode query (mention + context) and entity (title + description) independently using BERT; use FAISS to retrieve top-64 candidates by embedding similarity in O(log n) time.

quiz.explanation: The NIL problem: entity mentions that don't match any entry in the KB should be marked as NIL (not-in-KB) rather than incorrectly linked to a wrong entity. NIL detection strategies: (1) Score threshold: if best candidate score < threshold → NIL; (2) NIL classifier: binary classifier using mention + candidate features; (3) Contrastive approach: train with NIL examples explicitly.

quiz.explanation: ReFinED integrates mention detection and disambiguation in a single end-to-end model, while BLINK treats them separately. ReFinED's key innovations: (1) joint entity type prediction + disambiguation; (2) uses Wikipedia entity descriptions + structured types; (3) processes the entire document at once (not mention-by-mention). ReFinED is ~3x faster than BLINK on CPU while maintaining comparable accuracy.
